candidates.explanation: When a social login matches an existing user by email and that user is still inactive, this branch overwrites the account's provider and socialId with the social provider's values and saves them. A user who registered by email and hasn't confirmed yet can be converted into a Google account this way. A social login with the same email, even one made by someone else, triggers it. The provider stays 'google', so a later email login fails the `user.provider !== AuthProvidersEnum.email` check in validateLogin with `needLoginViaProvider:google`. The stock boilerplate just reuses the existing user here and never rewrites its provider.

register spreads the raw dto into usersService.create and never sets `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email`. The provider is left to defaults in UsersService.create and the entity, so it is not guaranteed to be 'email'. I can't see UsersService.create, so this is a weaker lead.

fix.description: In validateSocialLogin, remove the block that sets `user.provider = authProvider` and `user.socialId = socialData.id` for inactive users, so the existing user is only reused. If linking is really wanted, only do it after the email is verified and the account is active. In register, set `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` explicitly. Also repair any rows already switched to a social provider.

candidates.explanation: When a social login matches an existing user by email and that user is still inactive, this branch overwrites the account's provider and socialId with the social provider's values and saves them. A user who registered by email and hasn't confirmed yet can be converted into a Google account this way. A social login with the same email, even one made by someone else, triggers it. The provider stays 'google', so a later email login fails the `user.provider !== AuthProvidersEnum.email` check in validateLogin with `needLoginViaProvider:google`. The stock boilerplate just reuses the existing user here and never rewrites its provider.

register spreads the raw dto into usersService.create and never sets `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email`. The provider is left to defaults in UsersService.create and the entity, so it is not guaranteed to be 'email'. I can't see UsersService.create, so this is a weaker lead.

fix.description: In validateSocialLogin, remove the block that sets `user.provider = authProvider` and `user.socialId = socialData.id` for inactive users, so the existing user is only reused. If linking is really wanted, only do it after the email is verified and the account is active. In register, set `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` explicitly. Also repair any rows already switched to a social provider.
